prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage. Bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design.
2. One dominant flat block-colour background for the whole shot: lime green. Never a rainbow, never a gradient.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Never a recognisable person's face.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the background's contrasting colour. Real paper texture, print dots, small tape pieces.
5. Consistent upper-left light. Small paper-layer shadows only.
6. Everything is flat matte printed paper. No glow, no neon, no bloom, no halos, no luminous edges. Nothing emits light. Not glossy 3D. Not live action.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif, black or cream, printed on paper chips, large, safe margins. English spelling and letterforms accurate and stable. Only the headline text in the copy list, nothing else.
8. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window. One strongest visual focus at a time. No camera shake. Movement starts on the first frame; a small loop continues at the end. No empty frames.
9. Numbers, when specified, are printed complete from their first visible frame. Never counting up, never morphing, never redrawn.
10. No brands, logos, watermarks, or text beyond the copy list.
11. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
12. Identity anchor: rough white torn-paper edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: the three cards; a paper map shape; a paper hand.
Opens on the three cards, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The three cards slide together into a cutout map shape; a paper hand enters and holds it steady.
Ends holding on the held map.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "BRAZIL $77B".

COPY LIST: "BRAZIL $77B". Exact strings; nothing else appears in frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "The company has signalled a focus on Brazil's seventy-seven billion dollar sustainability market.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a 2D-animated modern editorial paper collage. The scene opens on <Picture 1>, which features a solid, flat lime green background. In the center, three black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts of people's faces are layered with rough white torn-paper edges and subtle shadows cast from an upper-left light source. Above them, a white paper strip with the text "WHAT CHANGES IT" is visible. Immediately upon the first frame, the action begins: the white paper strip with the text "WHAT CHANGES IT" quickly slides upward and out of frame, while the three photographic cutouts rapidly slide toward each other, merging into a single black-and-white halftone cutout in the shape of a map of Brazil. Simultaneously, a rectangular cream-colored paper chip slides in from the right with a slight overshoot, landing stably in the upper-right area with the headline "BRAZIL $77B" printed in a bold, black, sans-serif typeface. The text is clean, legible, and stable. From the right edge of the frame, a black-and-white halftone cutout of an anonymous paper hand enters quickly, moving with a snappy motion to overlap and hold the map shape steady in the center of the composition. The camera remains a Static Shot throughout. By the end of the 5-second duration, the composition holds steady on the paper hand gripping the map of Brazil and the "BRAZIL $77B" headline, with a very subtle, slow-pulsing scale loop applied to the map to maintain visual energy. All elements maintain a flat matte paper texture with visible print dots and small paper-layer shadows.

overall_soundscape: The audio is characterized by crisp, tactile foley sounds of physical paper. Distinct, sharp paper-slap sounds occur as the cards merge and the hand enters, accompanied by the short, sticky sound of adhesive tape being pressed down.
